searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight for chunk h4, none of them the author's; two left unspent. Two were restricted to the house's own domain and read through their summaries. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year and what it is the year of, the people and their dates, the village, the kind of producer, every change of hands, the grapes, the sites, the first vintage, the lees, the dosage, the bottle, the other cuvées, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile told as a present state, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash).
Every table line was read aloud as a captain would say it, for a claim no source carries.

tested.founded: 1976 the brand, 1972 the Centre Vinicole, 1986 the brand sold to it: the house's own story page. Confirmed.
tested.kind: CM read by the author from a label's traceability code through Open Food Facts; the house calls itself the brand of united growers. Stands.
tested.story: The house says Nicolas Feuillatte invested in the Champagne vineyard at forty and first made the wine for a circle of American friends; nothing on its pages says he inherited a family vineyard at Bouleuse, and one account says the house bought a vineyard there: the inheritance cut. The union's aim in 1972, by the house, was to help growers sell their surplus grapes; the record's make and keep their wine together was not found: reworded. The merger: both assemblies voted on 15 December 2021 and it took effect on 31 December 2021 (Decanter, the Drinks Business); Nicolas Feuillatte and Castelnau run as separate divisions. Confirmed.
tested.cuvee: First vintage 1985: Wine Spectator's vertical and a merchant, and Wine Spectator gives the 1985 as about three fifths Chardonnay, which the record leaves as accounts differ. At least ten years in the cellar for the Palmes d'Or range: the house (its 2009 page says nearly ten). The rosé: Palmes d'Or Rosé Intense, Pinot Noir alone from Bouzy and Les Riceys, by saignée: the house. The black bottle was not in this refuter's results; it rests on the house's pages as the author read them.
tested.table: house45 carried the inherited vines and the make and keep aim: both fixed. cuvee45, the sale and the ten and twenty second lines read aloud: each claim found in the record's sources.
tested.cards: Three cards and three questions read: one right answer each, plausible wrong ones (Belle Époque, Grand Siècle, Celebris; 1972, 1976, 2021; 1976, 1972, 1999), no length clue, explanations that teach.
